info.title: Sofa King server
info.description: The Sofa King media center server's HTTP interface: the API the Sofa King app uses under /api/v1 for live TV, recordings and media libraries, the admin API under /api/v1/admin, the player outputs under /output, the logo cache and the HDHomeRun emulation Plex reads. The admin portal's pages under /admin are HTML and are not described here, only this document's own route. Timestamps are UTC instants. The admin token is accepted on every route that takes the API token.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Public checks that take no token.

tags.name: Server
tags.description: The dashboard summary and this document. Bearer: the API token, or a read token for the summary; the document sits behind the portal's session.

tags.name: MCP
tags.description: The Model Context Protocol endpoint for AI assistants. Bearer: the admin token or a read token.

tags.name: Live TV
tags.description: The catalog and guide the app reads. Bearer: the API token.

tags.name: Playback
tags.description: Sessions that select a source and relay its media. Bearer: the API token; the media URLs take none.

tags.name: Sources
tags.description: Provider and source health. Bearer: the API token.

tags.name: Outputs
tags.description: The M3U playlist, XMLTV guide and player streams. Token: the output token as ?token= or a bearer, or the API or admin bearer.

tags.name: HDHomeRun
tags.description: What Plex reads from an HDHomeRun tuner. No token; clients are admitted by address (SOFA_HDHR_ALLOW and the addresses allowed at run time).

tags.name: Admin
tags.description: The server, its sessions, candidates, guides and the lineup. Bearer: the admin token, or the API token when none is set.

tags.name: Policy
tags.description: The lineup policy and its runs. Bearer: the admin token.

tags.name: Plex
tags.description: Plex Live TV sync. Bearer: the admin token.

tags.name: Viewers
tags.description: Pairing a client to the server and the preferences each client keeps on it. Bearer: the API token, except the pairing claim, which takes none.

tags.name: Library
tags.description: Media libraries: folders of movies, shows and other videos under SOFA_MEDIA_DIR, which the server reads and never writes. The app's routes take the API token; /artwork takes none; the admin routes take the admin token.

tags.name: Recordings
tags.description: The DVR: recordings and the series rules that schedule them. Bearer: the API token.

tags.name: Hooks
tags.description: Calls from Sonarr, Radarr and other tools when files change, each queuing a library scan. A hook token from POST /api/v1/admin/tokens, or the API or admin token, as a bearer, a Basic password or the X-MediaBrowser-Token or X-Emby-Token header.

tags.name: Watchlist
tags.description: The household's watchlist of library items and guide titles. Bearer: the API token.

adminToken.description: SOFA_ADMIN_TOKEN, or SOFA_API_TOKEN when no admin token is set. When an admin token is set, it also opens every route that lists apiToken, the hooks and the outputs among them, as the shared API token does: it is no paired device, so a PUT of preferences/{clientId} may write any client

outputToken.name: token
outputToken.description: SOFA_OUTPUT_TOKEN; also accepted as a bearer

deviceToken.description: A paired device's own token from POST /api/v1/pair; it opens what SOFA_API_TOKEN opens outside /api/v1/admin and /api/v1/hooks

readToken.description: A read token from POST /api/v1/admin/tokens; it opens the admin reads listed with it

hookToken.description: A hook token from POST /api/v1/admin/tokens; it opens the hooks and nothing else. Also accepted as a Basic password

mediaBrowserToken.name: X-MediaBrowser-Token
mediaBrowserToken.description: A hook token or SOFA_API_TOKEN, as Sonarr's and Radarr's Emby / Jellyfin connection sends its API key; X-Emby-Token works too

libraryKinds.name: Sofa-Library-Kinds
libraryKinds.description: The library kinds beyond movies, shows and videos the client shows, comma separated: music. Without music, Music libraries and their items are left out.

playbackProtocols.name: Sofa-Playback-Protocols
playbackProtocols.description: The live protocols the client's player plays, comma separated: hls, mpegts. A client that names no protocol, or hls alone, gets an MPEG-TS channel as an HLS playlist the server packages from the stream; hls, mpegts asks for the source's own format.

clientId.name: clientId
clientId.description: The client's own stable id: 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores.

outputName.name: name
outputName.description: A named output: 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

Error.description: An error: code, message and whether a retry may succeed.

JsonRpcMessage.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 request, notification, response or error, as MCP defines them

viewers.description: The server pairs clients (/api/v1/pair) and keeps their preferences.

watchlist.description: The server keeps the household's watchlist (/api/v1/watchlist).

onLater.description: The server lists upcoming movies, sports, kids' programs and premieres (/api/v1/guide/on-later).

household.description: The server keeps the household's shared favorites and hidden channels (/api/v1/household/preferences).

status.description: ok, or removed for an entry the lineup no longer has

ProgramFacts.description: What TMDB says about a live program; kind is empty, with nothing else set, when TMDB lists no program of that title or the server has no TMDB token.

endYear.description: When a show that has ended last aired

cast.description: The first few billed, in billing order

creators.description: Who created a show, or directed a movie

AdBreakState.description: Whether the session's player shows an ad.

remainingMs.description: How long the break has left, when the playlist says

url.description: Relative; resolve against the server address

providerId.description: The provider of the source the server picked

health.description: What the relay has seen of the session's media, on a read or a renewal; null when the session opens

sourceId.description: The source whose probe was put at the front of the queue.

dismissed.description: Taken off Continue watching by hand; the next play clears it.

lastPlayedAt.description: For a song: when it was last played.

unwatched.description: A show's or season's unwatched episodes.

playState.description: A movie's, episode's or video's watch state; null before it is started.

extra.description: An extra's kind; null for anything else. A client shows a kind it does not know as other.

tmdbId.description: A movie's or show's TMDB id, from its name, its .nfo or the TMDB match.

tvdbId.description: The TheTVDB id, from the name, the .nfo or TMDB's record of a show.

imdbId.description: The IMDb id, tt and digits, from the name, the .nfo or TMDB's record.

artistId.description: An album's or track's album artist.

trackArtist.description: A track's own artist when it differs from its album's, as on a compilation.

album.description: A track's album title; the album is its parentId.

next.description: The cursor for the next page; null on the last.

genres.description: Every genre in the library; empty on search results.

people.description: On search results, the cast and directors whose names hold the query, the most credited first; at most 10.

letter.description: An upper-case letter, or # for a digit or a symbol.

letters.description: Runs of items in title order by first letter, so their counts added up give where each starts; null when the request did not ask.

codec.description: A subtitle codec other than subrip, ass, ssa, mov_text, webvtt or text is pictures, drawn through subtitleIndex.

next.description: For a show, the episode to play next.

segments.description: Spans a player offers to skip, such as an episode's intro.

scrub.description: Thumbnails to show over the seek bar while scrubbing; null until the server has made them, or for a file under five minutes.

extras.description: A movie's or show's trailers, featurettes and other extras, trailers first.

related.description: For a movie, show, video or artist, up to 12 others in its library that share its genres, the most shared first; for an artist, the artists ListenBrainz's listeners play alongside them come first.

popular.description: For an artist, up to 10 of their songs that ListenBrainz's listeners play most, most played first.

ScrubThumbnails.description: JPEG sheets of columns by rows tiles, left to right and then down. Tile n overall, on sheet n / (columns * rows), shows the file at n * intervalMs.

sheets.description: Each sheet's path under /artwork, with its ?v= version.

watched.description: Set by hand; wins over the position. The only field a show or season takes.

dismissed.description: True takes a movie, video or episode off Continue watching, false puts it back; either leaves its position and watched flag.

audioCodecs.description: aac, ac3, eac3, mp3, opus, flac, dts, truehd

deepColor.description: The video codecs it also decodes at more than 8 bits a sample, such as hevc; null for a player that does not say, which the server takes as every codec in videoCodecs but h264.

itemId.description: The item to play; leave it out with recordingId.

recordingId.description: A running or finished recording to play instead of an item.

audioIndex.description: An audio stream index from the item's tracks; the file's default when null.

subtitleIndex.description: A picture subtitle track from the item's subtitles to draw into the picture, which converts the stream. A text track or a recording answers 400.

wholePlaylist.description: For a player that cannot restart a conversion: a transcode serves a VOD playlist of the whole item, with startMs 0, and converts from the segment the player asks for.

intent.description: A preview of a library item (a trailer behind a page) lasts 45 seconds past its last renewal and yields its conversion slot to a watch; a recording answers 400 for it.

Where in the item the HLS stream's time 0 is; 0 for direct play.

recordingId.description: Set, with an empty itemId, when the session plays a recording.

intent.description: What the session is held for; a server that does not know previews always says watch.

channelIds.description: Two to four different lineup channels, drawn left to right and top to bottom.

audio.description: The index in channelIds of the tile whose sound plays; it has a border.
Move the sound to this tile, restarting the stream under a new epoch.

hidden.description: Channel ids the client leaves out.

favorites.description: Starred channel ids, in the viewer's order.

updatedAt.description: Set by the server on every write.

favorites.description: Starred channel ids, in the household's order.

hidden.description: Channel ids the sharing devices leave out.

preferences.description: Null until the client saves some.

ownToken.description: Whether the client holds a token of its own from pairing; false means it uses SOFA_API_TOKEN.

slides.description: Image URLs fetched as each slide airs.

sessions.description: Live and library playback sessions open now.

updateAvailable.description: Whether a newer image is published; null until the update check has an answer.

id.description: The app's id for the crash, so a report sent twice is stored once.

frames.description: The stack trace's frames, at most 60.

gracenoteId.description: The policy's Gracenote station id for the station

allowed.description: Allowed from the portal or this API, kept in the database

channelId.description: The iptv-org channel id, such as CNN.us; required to accept

items.description: An IP literal or CIDR block

items.description: Present items by kind: movie, show, season, episode, video, artist, album or track.

scanOk.description: False when the last scan found the folder missing, or empty while the library held files.

unavailable.description: The folder was missing or empty, so nothing changed.

path.description: A file or folder, as the server names it or as SOFA_LIBRARY_PATH_MAP maps it.

libraries.description: The ids of the libraries whose scan was queued; empty when no library holds the path or the event changes no file.

reason.description: Why a recording failed or was cut short: MISSED, NO_MEDIA, STOPPED, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED and the like.

conflict.description: A scheduled recording that overlaps more recordings than the server has playback slots.

commercials.description: How far the commercial scan of a kept recording got; null when the server does not look.

breaks.description: The commercial breaks found, in order.

updatedAt.description: When the server last changed the recording; null from an older server.

startMs.description: From the start of the file.

usedBytes.description: What running and kept recordings use.

title.description: Matched against program titles, ignoring case.

channelId.description: Null records the title on every channel.

newOnly.description: Skip airings the guide marks previously shown.

keep.description: Finished recordings the rule keeps, newest first; 0 keeps all.

priority.description: The higher wins a playback slot when recordings conflict; a one-off outranks every rule.

match.description: A team or keyword rule's match; a title rule has none.

get.description:
The OpenAPI document, behind the portal's session

Served behind the portal's session, not a token.

303.description: To the portal's sign-in without a session

get.description: Public liveness check
Public database readiness check
Server ID, time, API version and capabilities (`catalog`, `guide`, `playback`, `events`, `viewers`, `library`, `recordings`, `watchlist`, `multiview`, `music`)

post.summary: Claim a pairing code for a token of the device's own
post.description:
Exchange a pairing code for a token of the device's own, see [pair a client](#pair-a-client); no token. 10 claims a minute per client address, then `429`

The code comes from the admin portal's Devices page or POST /api/v1/admin/pairing-codes; it is live for ten minutes and works once, and five wrong claims void it. The answer is a new token for this clientId, which revokes the one it was paired with before; forgetting the device revokes it. No bearer token: 10 claims a minute per client address, then 429. A server without an API token answers an empty one.

400.description: INVALID_REQUEST: a malformed claim or client id

429.description: Too many claims from this address

get.summary: The preferences this client last saved
get.description: The preferences the client with that id last saved, see [viewer preferences](#viewer-preferences); `404 VIEWER_NOT_FOUND` before its first save

put.description:
Replace that client's preferences; answers the stored document with the server's `updatedAt`. A token paired to a client writes only that client, `403 CLIENT_MISMATCH` otherwise; the shared API token and issued tokens without a client write any. A new client past 200 viewers answers `409 VIEWER_LIMIT`

Each list holds at most 1,000 distinct ids; an empty name or platform keeps the stored one. The answer is the stored document with the server's updatedAt. A token paired to a client writes only that client; the shared API token and issued tokens without a client write any.

403.description: CLIENT_MISMATCH: a token paired to another client

get.summary: The household's shared favorites and hidden channels
get.description: The household's shared favorites and hidden channels, see [viewer preferences](#viewer-preferences); an empty document with an empty `updatedAt` before the first save

put.summary: Replace the household's shared favorites and hidden channels
put.description:
Replace the household's shared favorites and hidden channels; answers the stored document with the server's `updatedAt`

Each list holds at most 1,000 distinct ids. The answer is the stored document with the server's updatedAt.

get.summary: The catalog: the enabled lineup entries as channels
get.description:
Catalog revision and the enabled lineup entries as channels; supports ETag/If-None-Match

Carries an ETag; If-None-Match answers 304.

post.summary: Programs overlapping a window for up to 200 channels
post.description: Programs overlapping a requested channel/time window

get.summary: Movies, sports, kids' programs or premieres coming up on the enabled channels
get.description:
Movies, sports, kids' programs or premieres coming up on the enabled channels

Programs that have not ended and start within days, soonest first. A movie needs a Movie or Film category beside a film genre and no News or Sports one; sports and kids match their categories; new is a Premiere category or a new airing of a season's first episode.

get.summary: What TMDB says about a live program
get.description:
What TMDB says about a live program, found by its exact guide title, for the break screen: `kind` (`show` or `movie`), `year`, `endYear`, `studio`, `seasons`, `episodes`, `cast`, `creators`, `tagline` and `rating`. `movie=true` searches movies first. Every field is empty when TMDB lists no such title or the server has no TMDB token; see [libraries](libraries.md#details-from-tmdb)

Found by its exact guide title, for the break screen to show a fact at a time. Every field is empty when TMDB lists no such title or the server has no TMDB token.

get.summary: Each provider's import status and counts
get.description: Provider import status and channel counts

get.summary: Every source's health and manual-disable flag
get.description: Health and manual-disable flag of every source

patch.summary: Disable or enable a source by hand
patch.description:
Set `manuallyDisabled`; takes the admin token, as the admin routes do

A disabled source is never selected or probed; sessions playing it move on.

post.summary: Open a preview or watch session
post.description:
Create a preview or watch session. A client that names no protocol in a `Sofa-Playback-Protocols` header (comma separated protocols), or names `hls`, gets HLS, packaged from an MPEG-TS channel; `hls, mpegts` asks for the source's own format (`SOFA_APP_STREAMS=source` makes the default the source's format); see [architecture](architecture.md#playback)

Picks the channel's first selectable source. A client that names no protocol in Sofa-Playback-Protocols gets HLS, packaged from an MPEG-TS source; hls, mpegts asks for the source's own format. Repeating a key returns the same session while it lives; a key reused with other parameters answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. At capacity the oldest preview, then an idle player session, yields; otherwise 429 CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED.

get.description:
Read the current playback descriptor, with the session's `health`: `bitrateKbps`, `stalls` and `sourceSwitches`, as on the portal's Watching now

Moves the session to the next selectable source, with a new epoch, when the current one stopped being selectable.

patch.summary: Renew the lease; optionally change the intent
patch.description:
Renew the lease and optionally change intent; the answer carries `health` too

A watch session expires 90 s after its last renewal, a preview 45 s. Send {} to renew alone.

delete.description:
Release the session; returns 204

Idempotent; cancels its upstream requests.

get.summary: Whether the session's player shows an ad
get.description:
Whether the session's player shows an ad, for engines without timed metadata that cannot read the playlist's `#EXT-X-DATERANGE` ad marks: `inBreak` and, when the stream planned the break, `remainingMs`. `aheadMs` is how much the player has loaded past the picture; see [architecture](architecture.md#playback)

The fallback for engines without timed metadata, which cannot read the playlist's EXT-X-DATERANGE ad marks: the server places the picture from the last segment the player fetched and aheadMs, how much it has loaded past the picture.

get.summary: A playlist, segment, key or live TS stream of the session
get.description:
Session-authorized HLS or MPEG-TS media. `{epoch}` is the descriptor's epoch and `{token}` a random token for one playlist, segment or key

No token: the random resource token authorizes it until the session ends or its epoch changes. An older epoch answers 410 STREAM_CHANGED; a source no longer selectable answers 503 SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; more than 12 requests at once answer 429.

200.description: application/vnd.apple.mpegurl, video/mp2t or the resource's own type

get.summary: The enabled lineup as an M3U playlist
get.description:
The enabled lineup as an M3U playlist for third-party players, see [player outputs](#player-outputs)

audio/x-mpegurl; tvg-id is the channel id, URLs use the request's Host. The stream suffix follows the protocol of the source the channel would play now; format=ts lists every stream as MPEG-TS. A channel with a Gracenote id in the policy carries tvc-guide-stationid, any other with a logo tvc-guide-art.

get.summary: The scheduled and running recordings as iCalendar
get.description:
The scheduled and running recordings as iCalendar

One event per recording over the window the DVR records, paddings included. A read token from POST /api/v1/admin/tokens works as ?token= too.

404.description: RECORDINGS_NOT_AVAILABLE: the server does not record

get.description:
The lineup's programs as XMLTV

From three hours ago to days ahead; the server's runtime setting applies when days is absent.

get.summary: A named output's channels as an M3U playlist
get.description:
A [named output](#named-outputs)'s channels only, as an M3U playlist

As /output/playlist.m3u, holding only the output's groups and channels; url-tvg names the output's own guide. Stream URLs stay under /output/stream/.

get.summary: A named output's programs as XMLTV
get.description:
A [named output](#named-outputs)'s channels only, as XMLTV

As /output/guide.xml, holding only the output's groups and channels.

get.summary: Open a player session for the channel and stream it
get.description:
Opens a player session for the channel and streams it

An HLS source answers 302 to the session's playlist; an MPEG-TS source streams video/mp2t here, and with format=ts so does an HLS source, remuxed. The session is released 60 s after the last media request.

parameters.description: The channel id, which the playlist's URLs follow with .m3u8 or .ts; the suffix is ignored.

Movies, shows and videos whose title holds `q`, then those with a cast member or director whose name holds it, then episodes by title; at most 50. `people` names those cast members and directors, the most credited first, at most 10
